title: An equation quadratic in e to the x, and single-term forms
intro: No calculator. Give exact values and show the work that leads to each answer.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain why the other factor in part A(i) gives no solution.

rubric.point: $e^x = -2$ is impossible because $e^x > 0$ for every real $x$
accept: $e^x$ is always positive, so $e^x = -2$ has no real solution
$\ln(-2)$ is undefined, because no power of $e$ is negative

parts.sample: The other factor gives $e^x = -2$. But $e^x > 0$ for every real number $x$, so no real $x$ makes $e^x$ negative: this root of the quadratic in $u$ gives no solution.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Rewrite $\ln(x^2 - 9) - \ln(x + 3)$ as a single natural logarithm with no fraction, for $x > 3$.

parts.label: C

rubric.point: The equation written as a quadratic in $2^x$ and factored: $(2^x - 2)(2^x - 4) = 0$

parts.sample: $4^x = (2^x)^2$, so with $u = 2^x$: $u^2 - 6u + 8 = 0$ and $(u - 2)(u - 4) = 0$. Both values are positive: $2^x = 2$ gives $x = 1$ and $2^x = 4$ gives $x = 2$.
